aboutUsPage1: Stitchit is an art group created in 2021 by visual artist Rufina Bazlova and curator Sofia Tocar. The group works on burning socio-political issues using the traditional technique of embroidery as a tool of resistance and dialogue. Stitchit involves different communities and individuals into the creation process and blurs the lines of authorship. Collective means all people, who take part in a project and activities organized by Stitchit.

newsTheLittleBirdP7: The international contemporary art festival Survival Kit is one of the largest contemporary art events in the Baltics, taking place in Rīga annually. It was started in 2009 as a reaction towards the global economic crisis, calling for a consideration of various survival strategies within the changeable world of today. Every year, the festival is dedicated to a new and significant social topic. Abandoned Riga buildings are often used to hold festival events in order to draw attention to their future potential for development.

TermsTitle: Terms of participation in the project
TermsB0: On this site, after confirming the conditions, you will receive detailed instructions that will guide you from the preparation stage to sending us your finished work.
TermsB1: By taking part in the project you become an "ambassador" of a prisoner and will receive a "portrait" of a political prisoner in Belarus. All fates are equally important in this project, and we would like to record all stories, so each political prisoner is embroidered only once. If we don't have your character's pattern ready yet, or he/she is already being embroidered, we will offer you another person. Rufina is the sole creator of all the pattern work, so the process of creating a new scheme can take 2-3 months.
TermsStr0: The work process is divided into several steps that you can go through at your own pace. However,
TermsStr1: we have set a time limit of 2 months
TermsStr2: . This should be enough if you do occasional embroidery on your free evenings (or even if you're just a beginner).
TermsStr3: If you don't finish your work in 2 months and tell us you need more time, we may drop you from the project and pass your hero to someone else. We regret these strict rules, but we need to create some boundaries so the project doesn't turn into chaos.
TermsStr4: If you decide to withdraw from the project for any reason, or
TermsStr5: if you won’t be able to finish
TermsStr11: After your registration,  your data will not be available to other users of the website. You can also choose to use your real name or pseudonym and administer your own profile.
TermsStr12: An important element of the project is photo documentation of your embroidery process and final work. These photos will be later used on the site and in other publications on the project. Therefore, we want to warn you about it in advance and ask you to take the quality of future photos seriously.
TermsStr13: Participation in the project is free
TermsStr14: and open to all who are willing to give their time and effort to create an embroidery. The cost of creating the work is at your own expense and will cost you the like price of two cups of coffee. The final idea of the project is to create a large-scale canvas with embroideries of all political prisoners, therefore, by participating in the project you are obliged to send us your embroidery and become part of a large mosaic of portraits, which will later be publicly exhibited in galleries and cultural institutions.
TermsStr15: At the end, we will also
TermsStr16: ask you to write a short comment about your experience
TermsStr17: embroidering a political prisoner and participating in the project. Embroidery is a slow-paced process that allows you to gain a better experience and understand the story you will be working on. We would love to hear your thoughts, as they may become an addition to your work.
TermsStr18: By accepting the terms, you are confirming your serious intention to participate in the project!
